items.question: Is intentional pitch/roll to collective/yaw pitch trim release (PTR) de-clutching permitted in flight?
options: Yes, but only above 1000 ft AGL
Only during autopilot testing on the ground
items.explanation: Intentional P/R – C/Y PTR de-clutching in flight is prohibited.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Limitations

items.question: After one autopilot channel has failed, when must AFCS upper modes be disengaged?
items.explanation: AFCS upper modes must be disengaged after one AP has failed, except during approach.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Limitations

items.question: Where may the RHT (Radar Height Hold) AFCS mode be engaged?
options: Only over flat surfaces clear of obstructions
items.explanation: The RHT mode may only be engaged over flat surfaces which are clear of obstructions.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Mode Limitations

items.question: Is the VNAV AFCS mode operative on the AFCS Control Panel?
items.explanation: The VNAV AFCS mode is inoperative on the AFCS Control Panel.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Mode Limitations

items.question: What is the Minimum Use Height (MUH) for the HDG hold mode outside of an approach, at airspeed above 55 KIAS?
items.explanation: HDG mode functional from 0 KIAS to Vne has an MUH of 150 ft AGL (airspeed above 55 KIAS); in HOV or below 55 KIAS the MUH reduces to 30 ft AGL, and it is 160 ft AGL during approach.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Modes Engaged Limits and Minimum Use Height

items.question: What is the Minimum Use Height for the ALT hold mode in HOV or below 55 KIAS?
items.explanation: ALT mode MUH is 200 ft AGL above 55 KIAS, reducing to 50 ft AGL in HOV or below 55 KIAS.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Modes Engaged Limits and Minimum Use Height

items.question: What is the functional airspeed range for the GSPD (Groundspeed) AFCS mode?
items.explanation: GSPD mode is functional from 30 kts GS to 220 kts GS.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Modes Engaged Limits and Minimum Use Height

items.question: What automatically limits the AFCS GSPD mode to keep within airspeed limitations?
items.explanation: The Airspeed Envelope Protection (AEP) function keeps the helicopter airspeed between Vmini and Vne minus 5 KIAS regardless of the groundspeed reference selected for GSPD mode.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Airspeed Envelope Protection (AEP)

items.question: During a coupled VS (vertical speed) mode descent, engaging above what rate causes the AFCS to hold the aircraft at the maximum quoted rate?
items.explanation: VS engagement above 2000 fpm (or below -1500 fpm) will result in the mode returning the aircraft to the maximum rates quoted (2000 fpm climb / -1500 fpm descent).
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — AFCS Modes Engaged Limits, Notes

items.question: At what range should the pilot select VOR APP versus VOR NAV in the event of invalid DME/FMS distance?
options: VOR APP below 10 nm, VOR NAV above 10 nm
VOR APP above 10 nm, VOR NAV below 10 nm
VOR APP always, regardless of range
VOR NAV always, regardless of range
items.explanation: In case of invalid DME/FMS distance, select VOR APP at ranges below 10 nm (18 km) and VOR NAV at ranges greater than 10 nm.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — VOR Limitations

items.question: What is the maximum glideslope angle for a coupled ILS approach on the AW189?
items.explanation: The helicopter is certified to carry out CAT I ILS approaches up to a 4-degree glideslope.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Coupled ILS Approach Mode Limitations

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for a coupled ILS approach up to 4 degrees glideslope?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for glideslope up to 4 degrees is 150 KIAS; maximum airspeed at DA(H) is 130 KIAS.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Coupled ILS Approach Mode Limitations

items.question: If the PWR LIM message illuminates during a coupled ILS approach before reaching DH, what should the pilot do?
options: Reduce airspeed as required to extinguish the message before reaching DH
items.explanation: If the PWR LIM message illuminates, the pilot should reduce airspeed as required to extinguish the message before reaching DH.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Coupled ILS Approach Mode Limitations, Note

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for a coupled VOR approach?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for VOR approach is 150 KIAS.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Coupled VOR Approach and Navigation Mode Limitations

items.question: What is the maximum rate of descent permitted during a coupled FMS approach?
items.explanation: Maximum rate of descent during coupled approaches is 1000 fpm.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — FMS Limitations

items.question: Following a single AMMC reset in flight, when must a DBU (DBU EXEC on MCDU) NOT be performed?
options: During SID, STAR terminal procedure or during approach
It may always be performed safely
items.explanation: In case of a single AMMC reset in flight, the DBU must not be performed during SID, STAR terminal procedure or during approach.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — FMS Limitations

items.question: What must be verified before flying a procedure loaded from the FMS navigation database?
options: Nothing, the database is always current
The currency of the Navigation Data Base and coherence of the FMS data with the procedure to be flown
items.explanation: The pilot must verify the currency of the on-board Navigation Data Base (NAV DB) and the coherence of the FMS data with the procedure to be flown.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — FMS Limitations

items.question: Why should landing or external flood lights not be selected ON when using the ADF?
options: They cause electrical interference with the transponder
ADF indication is not reliable when they are on
They interfere with the GPS antenna
items.explanation: Landing or external flood lights must not be selected ON when using the ADF, since ADF indication is not reliable under those conditions.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — ADF Limitations

items.question: What FMS lateral navigation modes can be armed via the AFCS?
options: VOR, VAPP, LOC, NAV, BC, NAPP
items.explanation: Armed lateral modes on the AW189 AFCS are VOR, VAPP, LOC, NAV, BC and NAPP.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — AFCS General Information

items.question: What condition characterizes the AFCS 'hover/low-speed' regime referenced by the Collective Safety Function LOW HEIGHT protections?
options: Airspeed below 53 kts or HOV mode engaged
Any speed with the gear down
items.explanation: Hover/low-speed condition characterizes operation with airspeed below 53 kts or with HOV mode engaged; cruise condition is characterized by airspeed above 57 kts.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Collective Safety Function, Note
